documents.text: Female. DOB 1980-05-11. Nurse. Nationality: South Korea.

Rheumatology. 6 months of symmetric polyarthritis of MCPs, PIPs and wrists, morning stiffness 2 h. RF 128 IU/mL, anti-CCP >300 U/mL. Hand X-ray: periarticular osteopenia, one erosion at right MCP2. Dx RA. Start methotrexate 15 mg weekly + folic acid, prednisolone 7.5 mg bridging. Treated latent TB in 2018 (9 months isoniazid).
Methotrexate 20 mg PO weekly (up-titrated); folic acid 5 mg weekly; prednisolone 5 mg daily.
CRP 2.4 mg/dL; ESR 46 mm/h; ALT 38 U/L; creatinine 0.66 mg/dL; WBC 7.8 x10^9/L; Hb 11.9 g/dL; hepatitis B sAg negative, anti-HBc negative; HCV Ab negative.

Methotrexate 20 mg weekly for 5 months, adherent. Tender joints 9, swollen joints 7, patient global 6/10. DAS28-CRP 5.1 (high). Prednisolone still 5 mg. Plan add biologic or JAK inhibitor (never smoker, no VTE history). Uses contraception (progestin implant). Chest X-ray clear.
Has not had a positive TB test re-checked since 2018 treatment. Not planning pregnancy.

Rheumatology. History and physical, comprehensive visit.

REASON FOR VISIT: Seropositive RA with persistent active synovitis despite methotrexate; work-up before adding advanced therapy.

HPI: 46F, nurse, with RF 128 IU/mL, anti-CCP >300 U/mL, RA diagnosed 2026-03 (symmetric polyarthritis of MCPs, PIPs, wrists; one erosion at right MCP2 on hand X-ray). Methotrexate started 15 mg weekly, up-titrated to 20 mg weekly on 2026-04-02, adherent, taken orally. Prednisolone 7.5 mg bridging, now 5 mg daily. Morning stiffness about 90 min. Persistent pain and swelling of hands and wrists, with difficulty gripping and with fine tasks at work. No fever, weight loss, or rash. No GI intolerance or mouth ulcers on methotrexate.

VITALS: Height 165 cm. Weight 68 kg. BMI 25.0 kg/m2. BP 122/76 mmHg. HR 78 bpm regular. Temp 36.7 C. SpO2 98% on room air. RR 14.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
1. Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, 2026.
2. Latent TB infection, 2018, treated with isoniazid for 9 months, completed.
No other cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, autoimmune or neurologic history. No diabetes. No prior malignancy. No VTE. No history of serious or recurrent infection.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY: Tonsillectomy in childhood. No other surgery.

ALLERGIES: NKDA.

MEDICATION RECONCILIATION (current):
- Methotrexate 20 mg PO weekly (started 2026-03 at 15 mg, 20 mg since 2026-04)
- Folic acid 5 mg PO weekly (since 2026)
- Prednisolone 5 mg PO daily (started 2026-03 at 7.5 mg, 5 mg since 2026-04)
- Progestin implant for contraception (since 2024)
Recently stopped: none. Isoniazid completed 2018 (9-month course for latent TB). No NSAIDs or other DMARDs used. No prior biologic or JAK inhibitor.

SOCIAL HISTORY: Never smoker (0 pack-years). Alcohol rare, under 2 drinks per month, advised to keep minimal on methotrexate. No recreational substances. Works as a nurse.
FAMILY HISTORY: Mother with hypertension; no known inflammatory arthritis or TB in the family.

GYN / CONTRACEPTION: Premenopausal. Light irregular spotting on implant, LMP about 2026-08-28. Not pregnant, not planning pregnancy. Urine hCG negative today.

ROS: Positive for joint pain, stiffness, fatigue. Negative for fever, night sweats, weight loss, cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, chest pain, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dysuria, rash, dry eyes or mouth, Raynaud, oral ulcers, headache, focal weakness or numbness.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
HEENT: no conjunctival injection, no oral ulcers.
CV: regular rhythm, no murmur, no edema.
Resp: clear bilaterally, no crackles.
Abd: soft, non-tender, no hepatosplenomegaly.
Skin: no rash, no rheumatoid nodules.
MSK: tenderness 9 joints, swelling 7 joints (bilateral MCP 2-3, bilateral wrists, right PIP 3). Reduced grip strength bilaterally. No deformity or ulnar deviation. Hips, knees, ankles, feet normal. Spine non-tender with full range.
Neuro: grossly intact.

DISEASE ACTIVITY: TJC 9, SJC 7, patient global 6/10. CRP 2.4 mg/dL, ESR 46 mm/h (2026-09-08). DAS28-CRP 5.1 (high). HAQ-DI 1.4. Hand X-ray 2026-03: periarticular osteopenia, one erosion at right MCP2. Chest X-ray clear.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Seropositive RA with high disease activity despite 5 months of methotrexate 20 mg weekly plus low dose prednisolone. Continue methotrexate, folic acid and prednisolone 5 mg for now. Plan to add a biologic or JAK inhibitor.
2. History of treated latent TB (2018). Order IGRA now and review the repeat chest X-ray; counsel on TB symptoms. Hepatitis B and C serology negative.
3. Mild anemia (Hb 11.9), likely related to chronic inflammation. Repeat CBC and iron studies with today's labs.
4. Contraception: progestin implant in place, not planning pregnancy. Follow-up in 4 weeks to review labs and the treatment choice.

NCT02714634.title: Clinical Trial Evaluating Methotrexate or Leflunomide + Targeted Therapy Versus Methotrexate or Leflunomide + Sulfasalazine + Hydroxychloroquine in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis and Insufficient Response to Methotrexate or Leflunomide
conditions: Insufficient Response to Methotrexate or Leflunomide

arms.label: Triple therapy
interventions: Drug: methotrexate or leflunomide + sulfasalazine + hydroxychloroquine administration

NCT02714634.brief_summary: Approximately, 40 to 50% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the most frequent inflammatory arthritide, are non responders to the consensual 1st line of treatment : methotrexate. In these patients, it is well demonstrated that the addition of other immunomodulatory drug(s) often results in a significant improvement. However, the best option regarding the drug(s) to add remains unclear. Rheumatologists are currently used to adding a targeted therapy, such as anti-TNFα, and more recently abatacept or tocilizumab. Triple therapy using 3 conventional disease-modifying drugs (DMARDs), methotrexate or leflunomide+salazopyrine+hydroxychloroquine could be an alternative option to targeted therapies, all the more as they have a more favorable safety profile and a much lower cost. Uncertainty remains regarding the superiority of targeted therapies on triple therapy in methotrexate or leflunomide insufficient responders (IR). Investigators decided to address this issue by performing a randomized controlled pragmatic trial.

NCT05428488.title: Efficacy of a Sequential Treatment Strategy in Rheumatoid Arthritis

sites.facility: CHU de Brest La Cavale Blanche

NCT05428488.brief_summary:
In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the consensual 1st line conventional synthetic disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARD) of RA is methotrexate (MTX). In case of contra-indication or intolerance to MTX, leflunomide is an alternative. If the treatment target is not achieved with csDMARD strategy, addition of a biological DMARD (TNF inhibitors, anti-Interleukin 6 (anti-IL6)), abatacept, or rituximab) or a targeted synthetic (ts) DMARD (JAK inhibitors) is considered.

Current practice is to start a bDMARD (biologic Disease Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs) and especially TNF inhibitors (etanercept or monoclonal anti-TNF antibodies) with the benefit of hindsight. However, abatacept and TNF inhibitors have demonstrated similar efficacy in patients with insufficient response to csDMARD (AMPLE trial).

Although abatacept has shown a very good tolerance profile that might be superior to other bDMARDs rheumatologists might be reluctant to use it as a first line bDMARD as there is a belief of a slower efficacy compared to other bDMARDs or JAK inhibitors. Indeed, in real world study, compared to TNF inhibitors it seems that discontinuation of abatacept is more related to lack of effectiveness than safety issues.

Investigators have hypothesized that first rapidly controlling the inflammation phase, using TNF inhibitors followed by abatacept to induce an immunological remission would optimize response and tolerance of ACPA positive patients with RA. To demonstrate our hypothesis, the investigaors propose a randomized controlled trial with one arm receiving an induction therapy for 12 weeks with a TNF inhibitor followed by a cell-targeted bDMARD (abatacept) and the other arm, receiving TNF inhibitors.

rules.rule:phase_PHASE4: 4상 연구로, 이미 허가된 치료를 실제 진료에 가까운 상황에서 더 살펴보는 단계입니다.
